text:
maya: Heads up — SLO alerts spiking for EU customers (p99 latency + errors). Traces show a big chunk of EU traffic suddenly routing to us-east-1. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:
liam: I see the same in routing logs. Looks like EU pool reported no available instance for variant 'r50-quant-p6' and policy allowed cross-region fallback. The fallback picked 'r50-nq' in us-east which has different tokenizer/kv semantics -> partial responses + retries.
ops-bot: Incident detected: cross-region-routing surge (EU->US) >2x baseline for customer_tier=enterprise at 02:14 UTC.
maya: Ugh. So we triggered cross-region fallback across variant families. Can we stop cross-family fallbacks until we ensure compatibility?
raul: Root cause sketch: a recent rollback removed EU quantized replicas (deploy at 02:05), autoscaler didn't replace them because min_instances was 0 for several dedicated pools after the rollout. Quota checks then marked EU as "no capacity" and routing policy allowed cross-region divergence.
niall: Quick mitigation: setting a routing override to disallow cross-region fallbacks for affected accounts and set fallback_mode=graceful to avoid aggressive retries. Pushing command now.
niall: ```sh
# pin customer to local region fallback-only, don't auto-diverge to other variant families
redwoodctl routing update --scope="customer:acct_789" --allow-cross-region=false --fallback=local_variant
```
devex-nerd: UX note: Console currently shows "fallback: allowed/disabled" but does not show variant-family compatibility. We should surface "requested_variant_family" vs "actual_variant_family" in rollout and route previews and warn when they differ.
liam: Also discovered a telemetry blindspot: routed request events don't include original_variant_requested in the trace tags, so it's hard to detect cross-family fallbacks in dashboards. Filing a ticket now.
maya: Operational plan: 1) apply temporary routing override for enterprise customers, 2) scale EU pool back up, 3) revert min_instances config to previous safe default, 4) notify affected customers. I'll send an interim status email.
raul: Post-incident action items (rough):
- enforce min_instances >= 1 for dedicated pools during active rollouts
- add circuit-breaker that prevents >N cross-region fallbacks per-minute per-customer
- add variant-family compatibility check to smart-routing decision path
- expose original_variant_requested in telemetry/event schema
- Console UX: add warning for cross-family fallback in rollout page
ops-bot: Deploy started by niall at 02:35 UTC (routing override + quickscale EU pool).
maya: Monitoring: after override + quickscale, EU->US routing dropped to baseline within ~7m. Errors subsiding. Will leave override for 30m and then evaluate. :thumbsup:
devex-nerd: Can we also add a small checklist in the rollout UX that flags "min_instances=0" as risky when toggling deployments? Would have prevented this.
liam: Agreed. Also let's add a metric to the dashboard: cross_region_fallback_rate_by_customer and an alert for >0.5% sustained.
maya: Good. Thanks all — follow-ups: telemetry ticket (#ENG-2148), UX ticket (#DX-678), infra guardrail (#INFRA-982).
